text: Worse than / a Slave [circular Lost Legacy wordmark, top left]
scene: One anime-style woman with centre-parted black hair in a low bun stands with her hands folded in front of her, wearing a white hanbok-style jacket with lavender collar embroidery and a bright red wrap skirt. Her brows are drawn together, her eyes are glossy with two pale blue tear streams running down her cheeks, and her mouth is pressed downward. A thin hand-drawn curved arrow beside the lettering points back toward her.
mechanism: A single tearful portrait paired with a blunt comparison phrase that frames her situation as lower than slavery, so the image supplies the victim and the words supply the shock.
composition: The figure fills the left 45 percent from head to below the waist while the lettering occupies the right half, a clean two-block split on pure white. The arrow sits mid-right and points down-left, bridging the words to the figure. No clutter, and the red skirt is the lowest, heaviest anchor.
typography: Four words in a casual black handwritten face on two lines, Worse than over a Slave, set at a similar letter height and stroke weight; the first line is the wider of the two. Contrast on white is maximal and the phrase stays readable at 160x90. It carries the emotional claim, while the title adds the comfort-woman subject and the second-person angle that the thumbnail never states.
colors: Mostly white background with black text; the single saturated block is the red skirt and ribbon, flanked by pale lavender and white clothing. Black hair gives a strong dark anchor at the top. Red here is clothing and carries no warning meaning.
psychology: Visible cues are knitted brows, wet cheeks, a downturned mouth and a lowered, inward pose with the hands clasped low. Together these read as distress and vulnerability; there is no direct gaze at the viewer.
partnership: The title is a second-person POV invitation about a historically specific group, whereas the thumbnail drops the 'you' and offers a comparison that is vaguer about who or what. The unanswered question is what could be worse than slavery, and the hand-lettered line adds shock the title lacks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black Slave lettering first, then the tearful face on the left, then the red skirt, with the arrow acting as a short return path to the face.
art: Flat-coloured manga-influenced illustration with clean line work and soft cel shading on the hair and tears. Anatomy and fabric folds are coherent and the white background keeps the face and text crisp at phone size.
strength: Face, text and arrow each occupy their own clear zone on a clean white field.
weakness: The thumbnail never signals the historical setting or the POV format apart from the clothing.
bottleneck: The comparison line gives emotion but no concrete setting cue for a browsing viewer.
action: Hypothesis: add one period cue such as a rice-paper door or a year stamp behind the figure and test whether it improves the sense of what the video covers.
counterexample: Seq 5 uses the same portrait-plus-handwriting template but with a bolder second line and a more provocative figure crop.
expression_label: tearful, brows knitted, mouth turned down
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A chibi-proportioned office worker with spiky black hair, half-lowered eyelids and a small closed smile walks down the aisle between two rows of cubicles, carrying a brown leather briefcase in one hand and wearing a lanyard ID badge. To his left a grey-haired man in a dark suit with an open mouth and a raised palm leans out from a cubicle. Two seated workers in the foreground face monitors at the left and right edges, and about nine more heads peek over partitions in the background.
mechanism: An early-exit visual: one figure walks away from a row of seated workers while a senior colleague reacts, implying the title's retire-young story without any words.
composition: The walker is centred and the largest element, framed by symmetrical cubicle rows that converge toward him like leading lines. The reacting older man is the secondary focus at left. The scene is busy but layered in depth, with the middle aisle left open as a path.
typography: No overlay text at all, so the whole message depends on the title. Nothing needs to survive at 160x90 except the central figure and the briefcase.
colors: A restrained grey-blue palette of cubicle panels, floor and ceiling lights with dark navy trousers and a pale grey shirt on the hero. Low saturation throughout; the plant and the water cooler give tiny green and blue accents. The central figure separates through value contrast against the lighter aisle.
psychology: The walker's slightly lowered lids and faint smile read as relaxed, while the older man's open mouth and raised hand read as surprised or objecting. No red or urgency colours are used.
partnership: The title states a full age-52 millionaire outcome in words, and the scene adds only the leaving-the-office moment, not the millionaire or 52 element. The unanswered question is how he got there, since nothing visible shows wealth.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: central walker's face and briefcase first, then the shouting older man at left, then the cubicle rows as context.
art: Clean western-comic style with uniform outlines and soft shading. Small background faces are repetitive but there is no melted anatomy; the floor reflection and cast shadow under the walker are consistent. The scene is complex at full size but the main figure stays clear when shrunk.
strength: The off-centre exit action gives a clear narrative moment with a readable central subject.
weakness: No wealth, number or age cue appears, so the money payoff lives only in the title.
bottleneck: Without any overlay text the grey, low-saturation palette gives little pull in a feed.
action: Hypothesis: add a short overlay such as an age number and one gold element, for example a cheque or key, and compare against this text-free version.
counterexample: Seq 8 states the money payoff directly with two labelled panels, which this image leaves entirely to the title.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A round-faced cartoon man with dark bags under half-open eyes and an open, drooping mouth presses both clasped hands under his chin at the left. A thick black curved arrow leaves his head and points right toward a globe whose continents are wrapped in several grey metal chains. Behind the globe, a red area graphic with a jagged top edge rises toward the upper right.
mechanism: Debt shown as a chained planet, with a visibly distressed character and a rising red graph adding the consequence while the headline closes the exit.
composition: The man occupies the left third and the globe the right two-thirds, linked by the arrow and the text in the top centre. The jagged red graph forms an upward diagonal behind the globe. The picture is dense but the main objects do not overlap each other. The source image is a 480x360 frame with black letterbox bars at the top and bottom.
typography: Three heavy black capitals in one line across the upper centre on white, with the largest letter height of any element. It stays fully legible at 160x90. The words say nothing about debt or the world, so the globe and chains carry that, and the title supplies the question.
colors: White background with black text, green and blue globe, grey chains and a saturated red graph block; the red works as the danger and bad-news cue. The man's skin tone and white shirt sit against the white background with only a thin outline separating them.
psychology: The bagged eyes, open mouth and tightly clasped hands read as anxiety or helplessness, and the red rising graph adds an urgent, alarmed undertone. These are cartoon cues only.
partnership: The title poses an open why-question about world debt, and the thumbnail answers with a verdict, NO WAY OUT, which escalates the stakes rather than repeating it. The globe-in-chains tells viewers the subject is global without naming debt.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: NO WAY OUT headline first, then the distressed face, then follow the arrow to the chained globe and the red graph.
art: Flat vector cartoon with consistent outlines; chain links have simple gradients and the globe is a believable object. At 480x360 the edges are soft and the file shows lower resolution than its siblings, but main shapes survive minification.
strength: Chained globe plus panicked face deliver the whole idea of being trapped by debt without reading.
weakness: The word debt never appears and the red graph gives no label, so the topic is implied only.
bottleneck: The low-resolution 480x360 source softens the line work and chains.
action: Hypothesis: put a small dollar sign or debt figure on the chains to anchor the topic, then compare against this unlabelled version.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses the same face-plus-arrow-plus-object grammar but keeps a calm face, so Seq 3 carries more distress.
expression_label: wide anxious eyes, open mouth, hands clasped under chin
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A bearded cartoon man with round glasses, brown hair going grey at the temples and a wide toothy smile stands at the far left in a black three-piece suit and holds out a golden trophy topped with a large gold dollar sign. A small plaque with unreadable lettering sits on the trophy base. He is cropped at the shins and stands on a white background.
mechanism: A numbered-list promise: the headline names three milestones and the smiling trophy holder frames reaching them as an achievement.
composition: The man and trophy fill the left third, while the three-line headline spans the right two-thirds and dominates by size. The yellow bar behind the first line starts right at the dollar sign, giving a thin overlap between trophy and text. Hierarchy flows from big lettering to the character.
typography: Five words over three lines in heavy black condensed capitals; the first line is set on a yellow highlight bar and the next two lines are larger on white. The line NET WORTH and the numeral 3 survive at 160x90. Almost all wording is a copy of the title's opening, and the title's takeoff points and change-everything hook are missing.
colors: White background, black text, a yellow highlight bar, gold trophy and dollar sign, and a black suit. A restrained black, white and yellow scheme in which the gold and yellow bar give the main accent. There is no red or alarm colour.
psychology: The wide grin, raised eyebrows and presented trophy read as pride and celebration, an aspirational rather than fearful cue.
partnership: The thumbnail text is nearly the title's first half word for word, so it mostly repeats what the title says; the image adds only the trophy metaphor. The unanswered question is what the three milestones are, which neither element reveals.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow-highlighted 3 RETIREMENT first, then the large NET WORTH MILESTONES block, then the trophy and smiling face at left.
art: Clean vector-style cartoon with a gold gradient and sparkle highlights on the dollar sign; the plaque text is illegible scribble rather than words. Proportions are coherent and the layout is simple enough for mobile.
strength: The numeral, yellow bar and large black capitals make the list promise obvious at a glance.
weakness: The text repeats the title and the cartoon trophy is a stock finance metaphor.
bottleneck: Thumbnail adds almost no information beyond the title, so there is nothing new to click for.
action: Hypothesis: replace the trophy with three stepped bars showing an ascending dollar value to test whether visible milestones raise the sense of progress.
counterexample: Seq 23 puts a contrast pair of cash stacks in place of a generic trophy, so the idea shows without the title.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: An anime-style woman with long wavy black hair wears a gold tiara with a bead chain, a gold-and-orange choker and a tan strapless wrap top. Her eyes are wet with tear tracks, her cheeks are flushed pink and her mouth is small and slightly downturned. The figure is cropped at mid-torso and the bust is drawn large and is the biggest area of skin tone. A hand-drawn curved arrow under the lettering points back toward her.
mechanism: A royal-looking, crying figure combined with a dehumanising two-word phrase, pairing a sensitive vulnerability cue with a shocking label.
composition: The figure fills the left half to the bottom edge, the face sits in the upper-middle of her block, and the lettering fills the right half with the second word much larger than the first. The curved arrow below the text sweeps down-left to her chest area. Plain white background keeps it uncluttered.
typography: Three words in handwritten black lettering across two lines; Breed is roughly twice the height of the small line above. High contrast on white and legible at 160x90. The wording is a quote-style hook that goes beyond the title, which refers to a concubine and why the role is bad.
colors: White background with black text, warm tan and orange body tones, flushed red cheeks, a gold tiara and black hair. Skin and clothing are close in hue, so separation comes from the heavy outlines. No alarm colours.
psychology: Wet eyes, blush and a downturned mouth read as distress and embarrassment, with a lowered, vulnerable pose. The crop and exaggerated bust emphasise the body over the face and may read as sexualised.
partnership: The thumbnail adds a shocking phrase that the title only implies through the word concubine. It escalates the grim framing, but the visible crown suggests a royal rather than a Biblical setting, which might leave the actual context unclear.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: large Breed lettering first, then the tearful face, then the tiara and chest area, with the arrow tying the words to the body.
art: Manga-influenced cel illustration with a few messy stray hair strands, wobbly clothing outlines and a skin-colour gradient that looks smooth. No object or anatomy errors are visible; the isolation on white keeps the figure readable on a phone.
strength: The oversized second word and tearful face create an immediate, easy read.
weakness: The crown-and-bust styling hints at sexual appeal and royalty and gives no cue of the biblical setting.
bottleneck: The body-focused crop risks drawing attention away from the message and is visually generic for the genre.
action: Hypothesis: test the same lettering with a head-and-shoulders crop and one scriptural prop such as a scroll or tent cloth to check whether setting clarity improves.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses a near-identical layout but with covered clothing and a gentler phrase, so it leans on distress rather than the body.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A brown-haired cartoon man with round glasses, a pronounced chin and a flat mouth, in a white hoodie and blue jeans, extends one long arm holding up a pink brain. Below the brain sits a pink piggy bank with wide eyes beside a stacked bundle of green banknotes, and a thick black curved arrow from the headline sweeps down toward the cash and the pig.
mechanism: A two-word noun-phrase label made literal: a brain hovering over a piggy bank and cash, with the cartoon host presenting it.
composition: Character on the left, headline in the upper right and the brain, pig and cash forming a descending diagonal toward the lower right. The brain's upper right overlaps the lower edge of the first letters of BRAIN (a pink fragment shows inside the R), and the arrow reinforces the same diagonal. White background keeps everything separate.
typography: Two giant black sans-serif words on two lines take up the entire upper right, legible even at 160x90. POVERTY BRAIN names the concept; the title's growing-up and hidden-cost angle is missing from the image.
colors: Black text on white with a flat pink brain and pig, bright green cash, a white hoodie and denim-blue jeans. Pink and green are the two saturated accents, set against black. No warning colours.
psychology: The half-lidded eyes behind the glasses and the flat mouth read as neutral or deadpan, while the brain held out reads as a presentation gesture. The cartoon face does not carry the emotion, so the concept carries the interest.
partnership: The title promises a psychological cost of growing up poor, and the thumbnail compresses that into a catchy label. The brain-above-savings imagery suggests a link between thinking and money that the title only hints, leaving the question of what poverty brain actually is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: POVERTY BRAIN first, then the pink brain, then the pig and cash via the arrow, then the character's face.
art: Flat vector cartoon in a sitcom-style design with uniform outlines; a faint grey shadow under the bank and cash. Object scale is playful and consistent. The strong shapes remain clear when shrunk.
strength: Oversized label plus brain and piggy bank explain the concept instantly.
weakness: The character's neutral face gives little emotional engagement and the growing-up angle is absent.
bottleneck: The brain overlaps the lower edge of the headline slightly, which crowds the first letters of BRAIN.
action: Hypothesis: give the character a visibly stressed expression or empty pockets to test whether adding feeling raises the personal stakes.
counterexample: Seq 3 uses a similar cartoon-plus-arrow-plus-object layout but with a strongly distressed face, whereas this row keeps a flat one.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon street scene with two contrasting men. At centre a blank round-headed figure in a navy cap lettered RHG, a green sweater and tan trousers walks calmly while holding up a phone that shows a green rising line chart. Left of him a sweating man in monogram jacket and sunglasses carries several shopping bags marked GUCCI past a red sports car, with receipts, crumpled paper and a wallet on the ground and two small onlookers at far left pointing. On the right are two houses with RENTED. signs and a beige sedan, and the background has a neon-lit skyline.
mechanism: A lifestyle contrast: the debt-laden spender trails behind a calm figure who looks at a rising chart, with money chasing him embodied by the phone graph.
composition: The calm figure is the large central subject and the sweating spender is a left-of-centre secondary focus. A walking diagonal from the left to the right leads past rented houses. The ground is strewn with props and the city backdrop is busy, producing a crowded, many-element scene.
typography: No overlay headline. In-scene lettering exists only as small props: RHG on the cap, GUCCI on bags, two RENTED. signs and neon shop signs, several with unreadable or garbled letter forms such as CIZN and SBAXT. None of it survives at 160x90.
colors: Warm sunset yellow, lilac and peach sky and neon pink, blue and purple skyline against a bright green sweater, red sports car and green chart. High saturation spread widely, with the green sweater as the strongest figure-ground separation.
psychology: The calm figure's relaxed gait and the other man's sweat drops and frown give a visible contrast of ease and strain; the pointing onlookers add a mocking social cue. No warning colour is used.
partnership: The title is a long POV statement about money chasing you, and the scene supplies a rich visual story but no words or number. Which man the viewer should be is unanswered, and the phone chart is too small to carry the title's reversal.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: green-sweater centre figure first, then the red car and sweating man at left, then the phone chart, with the neon skyline as backdrop.
art: Digital cartoon with strong depth layers; garbled signage letters, malformed words on paper and misspelled shop names are concrete signs of generated imagery. The background is dense; at phone size the central silhouette survives but the story props blur.
strength: Strong colour contrast and a clear calm-versus-strained pair give a rich visual story.
weakness: Too many small props and garbled lettering make a crowded read and no headline summarises it.
bottleneck: Without any overlay text the scene must be decoded from tiny props that disappear at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the two men, enlarge the phone chart and add a 3-word overlay to test whether a simpler frame improves comprehension.
counterexample: Seq 8 conveys a comparable rich-versus-broke contrast with big labelled numbers and far less clutter.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A vertical split frame shows the same cartoon man in a navy suit and blue tie twice. On the left, a dim blue-purple room, he has a grey-white face, wide eyes and a downturned open mouth, standing beside a heap of paper bills labelled RENT, CARD and LOANS with an OVERDUE stamp and a stained mattress on the floor. On the right, a gold-lit office with a skyline, he smiles with a bundle of green bills in his hands next to a grey sports car and a gold watch on the floor.
mechanism: A mirrored poor-versus-rich pair of the same character, with two label plates that state the paradox of high pay and no assets.
composition: A hard centre line divides the frame into two equal halves, and each character stands at the middle of his half, which gives strong symmetry. The two label plates sit at the top left and right, and the objects at the bottom corners (mattress, car and watch) anchor each side.
typography: Two rounded label plates in white-on-dark and dark-on-cream with condensed capitals; the figures $0 and $200,000 are coloured red and green. Four words plus two figures remain legible at 160x90. The labels give the title's $200k and own-nothing idea as numbers, with the $0 added visually.
colors: Cold navy and violet on the left against warm amber and gold on the right, with a red $0 and green $200,000 as semantic accents. The split in temperature is the strongest cue; red $0 acts as a loss signal. Green bills pop on the gold side.
psychology: The left face has wide eyes and a downturned open mouth, the right has a wide smile with raised cheeks; together these pose strain versus ease. All are cartoon cues; the grey faces are blank.
partnership: The title is a POV statement of a paradox, and the thumbnail turns it into a side-by-side with exact figures, so the numbers are repeated but the debts and mattress add a fresh detail. Which of the two states the video says is the real one is left open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: NET WORTH: $0 label first, then the sad face below it, then jump across the centre line to SALARY: $200,000 and the smiling face, then the car.
art: Cartoon style with consistent outline weight and warm and cool lighting on each half. Paper text on the bills is malformed (EARLLASE, THSDUNS, TITUDETG), a concrete artefact of generated lettering. Main shapes remain readable when shrunk.
strength: The split temperature and labelled figures make the paradox readable in a glance.
weakness: The bill papers carry garbled lettering and the two identical faces differ only slightly at small size.
bottleneck: Both halves are visually busy, so small props compete with the labels at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: delete the paper pile detail and enlarge the two labels to test whether an even simpler split reads faster.
counterexample: Seq 7 tells a similar contrast story in a single busy scene without any label plates, which makes it harder to decode.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A heavyset cartoon man in a white shirt with rolled sleeves and blue jeans stands at the left with his hands in his pockets, half-lidded eyes and a closed smile, while more than ten green banknotes fall around him. Beside him is a brown office desk with a computer showing a bar-and-line chart, a paper stack and papers on the floor, struck through by a large red X. A thick black curved arrow from the numeral 50 points back at the desk.
mechanism: Leaving the desk behind is made literal: cash rains on a relaxed character while the workstation is crossed out, and the headline puts a hard age on the exit.
composition: The character takes the left third and the headline takes the right 45 percent, with the numeral 50 as the largest element at lower right. The desk with the red X is the central secondary focus and the arrow links the number to it. White background and generous gaps keep the layers apart.
typography: Three words in ultra-heavy black condensed capitals across three lines, with 50 about twice the height of the first two lines. Contrast is maximal and the whole headline is readable at 160x90. It restates the title's before-50 promise and omits the once-you-understand-this hook.
colors: Black headline on white, green banknotes, blue jeans, a brown desk and a single saturated red X as the accent. The red X marks negation of work and carries no warning meaning. The character's white shirt is separated from the page by a thick outline only.
psychology: Half-lowered lids and a mild closed smile read as relaxed and self-assured; the falling cash adds a reward cue and the crossed-out desk a release cue. No fear or alarm cue is present.
partnership: The thumbnail compresses the title's age-50 claim into a three-word command, so the number is duplicated, while the X-ed desk and banknote shower add the visible how-it-feels of not working. What the thing to understand is remains unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: giant 50 and the stacked RETIRE BEFORE first, then the arrow to the crossed-out desk, then the relaxed man and the banknote shower.
art: Flat vector cartoon with even outlines and a soft ground shadow; notes tilt at varied angles and the desk perspective is plausible. No malformed objects. The silhouette and red X still read at phone size.
strength: The giant 50 and crossed-out workstation make a short, countable promise in a glance.
weakness: Falling cash plus a smiling cartoon is a stock retire-early trope with little to set it apart.
bottleneck: The banknote shower scatters the left side without adding a new idea beyond the headline.
action: Hypothesis: remove the falling notes and add a calendar or age badge on the desk, then test whether a single tighter symbol sharpens the claim.
counterexample: Seq 23 shows a savings-versus-spending pair of objects, so its idea shows in the picture rather than relying on one number.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: 1 TSP / OPENS / LEG / VEINS! [CLOGGED VESSEL] [CLEAR VESSEL]
scene: A metal spoon at the top pours a fine magenta powder into a tall glass of water on a kitchen counter, and a pink-red plume swirls through the lower half of the glass. At right two cutaway tubes are stacked: the upper is labelled CLOGGED VESSEL and shows yellow lumpy deposits narrowing the channel between red blood cells, while the lower is labelled CLEAR VESSEL and shows only red blood cells in an open channel. The background is a blurred beige kitchen with a faint plant.
mechanism: A hidden-ingredient demonstration where one spoonful dissolving in a glass is linked to a clogged-to-clear body graphic, with the headline asserting an action on leg veins.
composition: The glass is a central vertical hero between the left text column and the right-hand tube pair, so the picture reads left to right as text, powder, result. The top tube is slightly larger and sits higher, creating a downward step to the clear one. All three zones are separated, though the three elements fill nearly the whole frame.
typography: Five words stacked on four lines in huge black capitals, with 1 TSP on a bright yellow rectangle and an exclamation mark after VEINS. The left half of the frame is filled by type and it stays legible at 160x90, while the small CLOGGED VESSEL and CLEAR VESSEL labels at right are unreadable at that size. The title's warning about plain water and the age 60 is not repeated.
colors: Hot magenta and red against a neutral beige blur, with a yellow headline bar and yellow fatty deposits as the contrasting accent. The red tubes and pink plume share a hue, so the powder is linked to blood visually. Saturation is high and the glass is separated from the background by the dark plume.
psychology: No person appears, so there are no face or gaze cues. The yellow highlight and exclamation mark carry urgency, and the clogged-versus-clear pair carries a fear and relief cue.
partnership: The title supplies the plain-water warning, the age 60 and the instant claim, while the thumbnail adds a dosage, a body part and a visual proof pair. The thumbnail promises a cure effect from a spoonful that the title only hints at, and it never says what the powder is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow 1 TSP bar first, then the pink plume in the glass, then the CLOGGED versus CLEAR tubes on the right, and finally the large OPENS LEG VEINS lines.
art: Glossy photographic-style render with shallow depth of field and a smooth powder-in-water plume, and a stylised 3D cutaway artery with consistent lighting. No distorted objects are visible; the tubes look like a medical illustration set against a photo-like scene.
strength: One glass and two labelled vessels turn a spoon-and-water claim into a clear before-after logic.
weakness: The cutaway shows a fatty-plaque artery while the text says leg veins, and the claim is stated as an action rather than a possibility.
bottleneck: The effect claim is stronger than the tiny CLOGGED and CLEAR labels can support at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: soften OPENS to HELPS and enlarge the vessel labels, then compare against the current wording to test whether it keeps the pull with less overclaim.
counterexample: Seq 19 is a plain text screenshot with no demonstration object at all, the opposite of this image.
hero_object: pink powder dissolving in a glass
medical_notes: Packaging implies a spoonful opens clogged leg veins instantly and pairs it with an arterial-plaque cutaway, with no source or qualifier shown.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with short dark hair, rectangular glasses and a navy suit leans forward with one hand cupped beside his mouth while his other arm extends to point at a green paper shopping bag. His brows are lowered and his eyes are narrowed behind the glasses. The bag carries a repeating monogram pattern with a large interlocking L and V and scattered O and G letters, and a black curved arrow at the lower right points toward it.
mechanism: A listicle promise with a stage-whisper gesture: the character appears to share a secret about luxury goods while the bag is flagged by both his finger and an arrow.
composition: The man occupies the left third and the bag the lower right; the headline spans the top right. His pointing arm and the arrow converge on the bag, giving two directional cues to one target. The white field is clean, so each of the three objects separates well.
typography: Five words over two lines in heavy black rounded capitals with a thick outline, sized to fill the top-right width. The numeral 10 and FAKE RICH remain readable at 160x90. The text reuses the key phrase of the title but omits the cosplaying-success angle.
colors: Black headline on white, dark navy suit, brown skin tones and a muted forest-green bag as the sole colour block. The palette is tight and calm, and the green bag pulls the eye by being the only saturated element.
psychology: Narrowed eyes, lowered brows and a hand held to the mouth read as conspiratorial or knowing; the forward lean and pointing add an accusatory cue. No red or alarm colours appear.
partnership: The thumbnail repeats the title's ten-signs-and-fake-rich wording and adds one concrete example, the designer-style bag, while the other nine signs stay unknown. The title's Archetypes and Cosplaying Success framing is not shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: top headline first, then the pointing hand, then the green monogram bag, with the man's squinting face last.
art: Clean flat cartoon with consistent outline weight. The bag's monogram letters are simplified imitation shapes with a few stray O and G letters, so it reads as a generic luxury-bag symbol; anatomy of the hand and pose is coherent. High legibility at small size.
strength: Pointing hand, arrow and bag make the single focal target unmistakable.
weakness: The scene shows only one sign of ten and the bag reads as a cliche luxury cue.
bottleneck: The wording largely repeats the title, so the picture alone has to deliver the new information.
action: Hypothesis: replace the bag with three small contrasting items, for example a rented-car key and a card, and test whether showing several signs better supports the number 10.
counterexample: Seq 24 pairs one portrait with a concrete dollar figure, whereas this image offers only a count and a generic prop.
expression_label: narrowed eyes, lowered brows, hand cupped at mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A large stick figure with a round white head, wide eyes glancing sideways and an open mouth showing a pink tongue points a thick finger toward a lioness lying on a grey blanket. A much smaller stick-figure baby with a laughing open mouth sits against the lioness's muzzle, and the lioness has closed eyes and a lowered head. The savanna background has several flat-topped acacia trees, a waterhole at right, yellow grass and a blue sky.
mechanism: A surprise-reaction pairing: an astonished observer points at an unexpectedly gentle scene between a baby and a predator, which raises the question of how animals treat young.
